name: brand-ai-readiness-audit
description: Audits a website for the problems that keep a brand from being found and cited by AI assistants, and from holding the visitors who do arrive. Emits one evidence-backed report of findings plus prioritised, mechanism-sound suggested actions.

skills.summary: Runs the pipeline, composes every other skill's output into the single audit report, validates it against the schema, and renders JSON, Markdown, HTML and PDF.
Normalises and safety-gates the target URL: canonicalisation, SSRF defence, DNS resolution, per-hop redirect revalidation, robots.txt policy, scope and budget.
Determines whether a crawler can obtain and read the pages: discovery, deep sitemap.xml audit, JavaScript render-fault diagnosis, indexability and canonical checks.
Selection-layer eligibility: structured-data validity and appropriateness, organisation completeness, sameAs breadth and entity disambiguation.
Absorption-layer readiness: evidence genres, structural legibility, and the Q&A-format trap, calibrated against the paper's measured influence quartiles.
Trust signals: datestamp presence and honesty, staleness by page type, and load-bearing claims asserted without corroboration.
The on-site half: answer-first orientation, intent continuity for AI-referred visitors, interstitials, scannability and summariser legibility.

The in-loop critic. Verifies evidence sufficiency, threshold coherence, sample sufficiency, claim-level discipline and known false-positive traps; drops, downgrades and merges findings; adds the proactive layer.

runtime.note: Standard library only. No pip installs, no external services, no model weights. The marketplace resolves entirely from its own contents.

network.scope: the registrable domain of the supplied URL, plus its robots.txt and sitemap

safety.ssrf_protection: private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, reserved and metadata address space blocked; every redirect hop revalidated

grounding.primary_reference: Zhang K., He X., Yao J. (2026). From Citation Selection to Citation Absorption: A Measurement Framework for Generative Engine Optimization Across AI Search Platforms. arXiv:2604.25707v2.
supporting_references: arXiv:2607.14035 — a survey of 45 GEO studies. Supplies the extractable-fact genres (prices, visible dates), the graded lever table used to label suggested actions, and the retrieval-backfire results.
arXiv:2609.07559 — shows page-quality scores correlate only weakly with citation (Spearman ≈ 0.11). The absorption proxy is therefore documented as a quality filter, not a citation predictor.
arXiv:2605.25517 — 252k-trial study; corroborates that prices and recent timestamps help extraction.
grounding.claim_discipline: Where a lever is measured with an effect size (arXiv:2604.25707) the report cites the figure; where a lever is only graded (arXiv:2607.14035 §7.5 Table 4) the report cites the grade. The two are never blended into one number or one chart.
